references.title: Perception and modification of plant flavonoid signals by rhizosphere microorganisms.

findings.statement: The review proposes that flavonoids shape rhizosphere communities through carbon availability and toxicity; this is ecological context for catabolism.
findings.supporting_text: they represent a potential source of carbon and toxicity

reference_review.review_notes: Abstract reviewed; use only ecological scope supported there.

references.title: Bacterial species involved in the conversion of dietary flavonoids in the human gut.

findings.statement: The review organizes intestinal flavonoid conversion by species, strains and enzymes; it is comparative background rather than an assay of Fde proteins.
findings.supporting_text: species and strains as well as their enzymes catalyzing the underlying reactions

reference_review.review_notes: Abstract and accessible review excerpts inspected; immutable local cache is abstract-only. No Fde late-step assignment derived.

findings.statement: The review surveys genes and enzymes of plant-toxin breakdown; its broad ecological coverage does not establish a particular Fde reaction.
findings.supporting_text: with an emphasis on the genes and enzymes involved in breakdown pathways

reference_review.review_notes: Abstract and publisher flavonoid section inspected; local cache remains abstract-only. Broad review is not an Fde-specific enzyme assay.

references.title: Naringenin degradation by the endophytic diazotroph Herbaspirillum seropedicae SmR1.

findings.statement: The fde locus is induced by naringenin and chrysin; whole-locus perturbation does not identify the molecular work of each encoded protein.
findings.supporting_text: its expression is induced by naringenin and chrysin, two closely related flavonoids

reference_review.review_notes: Full author copy read; access and the probable polar insertion are documented in module notes. The supporting quotation covers induction; the other findings rely on full-text observations documented there.

references.title: Genetic and functional characterization of a novel meta-pathway for degradation of naringenin in Herbaspirillum seropedicae SmR1.

findings.statement: FdeE mutant retention of naringenin and FdeC mutant accumulation of hydroxylated substrate support ordered entry hydroxylation and A-ring cleavage. They do not establish all downstream enzyme assignments.
findings.supporting_text: that is subsequently dioxygenated and cleaved at the A-ring by the FdeC

reference_review.review_notes: Abstract and publisher supplementary descriptions inspected; full text remains unavailable. FdeG interpretation is still pending.

references.title: Novel enzymatic route to the synthesis of C-8 hydroxyflavonoids including flavonols and isoflavones.

findings.statement: Purified FdeE hydroxylates flavonoids with NADPH. Its activity without added FdeD does not support an obligatory FdeD-to-FdeE relay; broad assay substrate acceptance does not prove native complete catabolism.

reference_review.review_notes: Cached full text inspected; retain recombinant assay versus native pathway distinction.

references.title: An isoflavone catabolism gene cluster underlying interkingdom interactions in the soybean rhizosphere.

findings.statement: Variovorax IfcA/B and redundant downstream IfcD1/D2 cupins support a related A-ring pathway with distinct substrates and unresolved X2-to-X3 chemistry. Its hydrolase mutant does not establish FdeB necessity.
findings.supporting_text: Gene disruption of locus 59470 did not affect the daidzein degradation ability.

reference_review.review_notes: Full text inspected. Supplementary identity mapping remains necessary before transferring the downstream cupin position to FdeH.

references.title: A NodD-like protein activates transcription of genes involved with naringenin degradation in a flavonoid-dependent manner in Herbaspirillum seropedicae.

findings.statement: FdeR responds to multiple flavonoids. Regulatory induction and ligand binding do not establish that each ligand follows every modeled catabolic step.
findings.supporting_text: FdeR binds naringenin and chrysin as shown by isothermal titration calorimetry

reference_review.review_notes: Cached abstract inspected; direct regulator-ligand assay supports induction context, not each catalytic assignment.

references.title: The Modification of the Flavonoid Naringenin by Bradyrhizobium sp. Strain ORS285 Changes the nod Genes Inducer Function to a Growth Stimulator.

reference_review.review_notes: Abstract cached; publisher Results and Figure 8 text independently inspected through indexed full text. Whole-operon deletion supports the ORS285 locus, not each enzyme assignment or USDA110 activity.

findings.statement: Naringenin-induced growth persists after fde deletion in ORS285, separating growth stimulation from catabolic evidence.
The ORS285 study reports naringenin degradation and a separate modification product; individual late Fde reactions are not resolved.
findings.supporting_text: Although strain ORS285 was able to degrade naringenin

note: Nine references integrated into module with per-step evidence and explicit assay boundaries. Optional context does not assert FdeD/FdeH dispensability.
